prompt:
You are reading one chemical structure image and writing down the molecule it depicts, as SMILES.

This is a blind test: read the structure from the drawing itself.

Guidance:
- Look at the image carefully, region by region. Count ring vertices and chain carbons one at a time, and check every heteroatom label, charge and bond order.
- Include stereochemistry (@/@@, /, \) only where the drawing actually shows wedges/hashes or cis/trans geometry. A carbon that is a stereocentre by connectivity but is drawn with plain bonds gets no stereo.
- Expand any abbreviation you can read (Me, Et, Ph, Boc, Ac, OMe, Ts, Bn, CF3, NHAc, etc.) into explicit atoms.
- Before answering, check that your SMILES is valid and that it describes the drawing atom for atom.
- Give one answer even if you are not certain of it.

End your response with exactly one line that starts with "SMILES: " followed by the bare SMILES string, with nothing after it. For example, for ethanol the last line would be:
SMILES: CCO

points: Sonnet 5.5 reading drawings that use TEXT SUPERATOMS (OMe, Boc, CF3, CO2Et, OTBS, Ts ...), one plain Messages API call per image: the PNG and the fixed prompt v2 below, no tools, no shared context, max_tokens 64,000, streamed. Image files have neutral names (sa_0001 ...) and no metadata.
Scored exactly like the other Sonnet tabs (sonnet_batch.verdict): RDKit canonical SMILES of the answer against the FULL molecule, every superatom expanded. Exact / stereo-only / wrong / unparseable.
Synthetic and real drawings are separate sections with separate exact rates; never pool them.

Molecules where abbreviations genuinely apply: corpus molecules with at least two condensable groups (chosen for label variety, all already read plain by the API-only arm), plus PubChem compounds picked for protecting groups and common superatoms (Boc/Cbz/Fmoc amino acids, silyl ethers, tosylates and triflates, nitroarenes, CF3 drugs, esters, acetylated and benzylated sugars).

Drawn with RDKit's CondenseMolAbbreviations (maxCoverage 0.8) over RDKit's defaults plus Boc, Cbz, Fmoc, TMS/TBS/TIPS/TBDPS (and their O- forms), Ts/OTs, Tf/OTf, OMs, SO2Me, Bn/OBn, Bz/OBz, OPMB, Ph, OCF3, CO2Me, CO2Bn, CO2tBu, NMe2, NEt2, NHMe. Boc, Cbz and Fmoc may only sit on N (a tert-butyl ester reads CO2tBu); RDKit's own 'iBu' (really sec-butyl) and 'iPent' are corrected.

Same renderer settings as the corpus (1500 px, scaled type and strokes). Each drawing passed: at least two labels; the condensed molecule expands back to the original exactly (canonical isomeric SMILES); every label is drawn as text; no two labels overlap.
The paired comparison uses each corpus molecule's plain corpus drawing, as read by the Sonnet 5.5 API only arm (same model, no tools).

Published drawings from the MolScribe real-image benchmarks (USPTO, CLEF-2012, UOB, ACS; huggingface.co/yujieq/MolScribe real.zip), truth = the benchmark's own full SMILES. All 8544 images were screened by Haiku 5.5 (one call each, $1.49) for text labels standing for two or more atoms; a label counts only if it maps to a known group AND that group is in the truth, and an image with any known label missing from its truth is dropped. Candidates: CLEF 217, UOB 64, USPTO 1525, acs 127. Sampled at random, half with two or more verified labels where available: ACS 40, CLEF 70, UOB 30, USPTO 200. Renamed rs_NNNN, re-saved as pixels only. UOB (Maybridge catalogue art) and ACS (journal figures) count in the metrics but are not shown; USPTO and CLEF drawings come from patents and are shown. Truth SMILES with R groups or dummy atoms are excluded.
